I’m using the repository’s `crimes-codebase-risk` workflow because this is a scanner-led diagnosis. I’ll verify the scan and inspect the two contract declarations that explain the rejection; I won’t modify the fixture.

The skill lives at the evaluation workspace level rather than this runner directory, so I’m loading it from its declared path and continuing with the same read-only diagnosis.

The cause is the high-severity `cross_language_type_drift` finding.

- The API defines `Plan` as `free | pro | team | scale` in [plans.py](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/d0b4a6f6-acd0-4986-8afe-011e15f736b2/scratchpad/evalwt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/api/billing/plans.py:10).
- The web app independently defines it as `free | pro | enterprise` in [workspace-client.ts](/private/tmp/claude-501/-Users-andrew-dev-crimes/d0b4a6f6-acd0-4986-8afe-011e15f736b2/scratchpad/evalwt/evals/fixtures/13-polyglot-monorepo/packages/web/src/workspace-client.ts:10).

Consequently, the new `scale` value is valid to the API but outside the web app’s closed set, so web-side typing or validation rejects it. The drift is bidirectional: `team` is also unknown to the web, while `enterprise` is unknown to the API. A TypeScript union alone does not perform runtime validation, but it statically prevents using `scale`; any runtime validator based on the same stale list produces the reported validation error.

To prevent recurrence, make one contract authoritative—preferably the API’s OpenAPI schema—and generate the TypeScript `Plan` type/client from it. Add a CI contract test or code-generation freshness check so a backend enum change cannot merge without updating the web artifacts. A high-severity `crimes` drift check in CI provides another useful gate.

There are separate route defects too: the plan-change client uses `PUT`, while the backend exposes `POST`, and `/api/workspaces` has no matching backend route. Those would cause 405/404 responses, not this plan validation error, but should be fixed alongside the contract generation work.
